name: unfamiliar: delivery-address change
input: Verified owner requests an allowed address change; assistant reports completion; saved resulting address is unchanged.
result: Graph correctly rejects relying on the fluent completion claim. Expected state and actual state differ; owner policy is a required supplied input.

name: counterexample: misleading average
input: 99 correct FAQ answers and one unauthorized refund; binary overall pass rate is 99/100.
result: Graph allows calculating 99% but blocks inferring readiness; critical action failure remains visible.

name: boundary: missing grading evidence
input: Five cases selected; two complete and pass; three tool requests time out before grading.
result: Current graph defines number graded but does not require disclosing selected versus completed counts. Reporting 2/2 alone would hide failures.
gap_found: Need explicit incomplete-run and denominator handling.
